notes:
Summary / context:
- Enterprise fintech platform building customer-facing AI assistant + embeddings for search/ranking. Concerned about both p95 latency under load and deterministic throughput for SLAs to their customers.
- Primary ask: reserved GPU pool across 2 regions (us-east-1, us-west-2) with AZ distribution and failover headroom. Want committed throughput guarantees and playbooks for cross-region failover.
Key technical targets and constraints:
- Target latency: chat p50 <= 3ms token-generation (edge of model/infra combo), p95 <= 40ms for 512-token prompts in dedicated mode (internal target).
- Throughput: baseline concurrent capacity for 12k tokens/sec sustained global; spike handling to 25k tokens/sec for 5-minute windows.
- Target failover headroom: reserve ~30% spare GPU capacity per region to handle AZ failure + graceful degradation paths for larger region outages (failover to secondary region with 20-30s warm-up).
- GPU mix: preference: H100 for hot serving pools, A100 for cost-optimised batch/embeddings pools. Customer asked for explicit per-GPU performance numbers and token/sec guarantees for quantized 4-bit and mixed-precision models.
- Caching: wants KV cache replication strategy across AZs and plan for prefix-cache warming during failover to avoid long cold-start latencies.
- Routing: smart routing policy required to keep sub-10ms regional latency for NA customers; fallback model variants allowed when capacity constrained.
- Autoscale/burst: needs deterministic burst policy - reserved baseline + documented burst capacity (monthly cap + true-ups).
SLA negotiation points noted in call:
- Committed uptime for dedicated pools (target 99.95%) and latency SLOs per model class. Customer expects SLA credits tied to throughput shortfalls, not only availability.
- Maintenance windows: prefer asynchronous rolling upgrades with at least 72-hour notice and canaries limited to 1-2% of traffic.
POC plan (agreed):
- Step 1: baseline perf runs (48h) using their synthetic workload (chat + reranking mix), measure token/sec and p95 latencies per region for H100/A100.
- Step 2: simulate AZ outage by draining an AZ and measuring failover time, KV-cache warm-up and effective throughput drop; measure p95 during warm-up.
- Step 3: run cost / reservation model: quantify reserved GPU counts by region for three headroom scenarios (20%, 30%, 50%) and estimated monthly committed spend + burst allowances.
- Step 4: draft SLA appendix (throughput SLOs, measurement windows, credit math) for legal procurement.
Open questions for Redwood team:
- Exact kernel/optimizer profiles used for 4-bit quantized variant; need per-model benchmarking artifacts.
- Mechanism for cross-region KV cache replication and expected warm-up latencies (docs requested).
- Formal definition of 'throughput guarantee' (sustained tokens/sec vs 95th-spike handling).
Customer quotes / voice snippets:
- "We need predictable capacity — our SLAs to banks can't wobble during peak trading hours."
- "If region goes down we expect at most a small degradation window, not a total outage."
Next immediate actions (owner on each):
- SE (Lucas): schedule perf scripts + kickoff POC by 2026-03-03.
- AE (Maya): deliver draft commitment language and high-level reserved GPU plan for finance review (by 2026-03-10).
- Solutions: produce H100 vs A100 benchmark table and headroom cost scenarios (due 2026-03-08).
